lines.en: label dormwarsfive8:
scene courtroomcontest1
: For the honorable judge Imani Imai to preside over the case of Kumon-mi vs. Wakana Watabe!
lines.zh: : 现在，有请尊贵的法官 Imani Imai 主审本案：Kumon-mi 市 诉 Wakana Watabe！

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest2
: You may now be seated.
lines.zh: : 各位现在可以就座。

lines.en: : Ya didn’t give any of us chairs!
lines.zh: : 你根本没给我们椅子！

lines.en: : That’s not true...the jury and...the lawyers have them...
lines.zh: : 不是这样的……陪审团和……律师们有的……

lines.en: : Oh, so the common man gets screwed over again! Typical justice system!
lines.zh: : 哦，所以普通人又被坑了！典型的司法系统！

lines.en: : Damn it. Starting to think I should’ve appointed a bailiff if y’all are just gonna be talking the whole time.
lines.zh: : 该死。我开始觉得，如果你们全程都要插嘴，我真该任命一个法警。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest3
: Regardless! Today’s trial will serve to determine whether or not one Wakana Watabe is guilty of crimes against humanity. Specifically that of the custodial variety.
lines.zh: : 不管怎样！今天的审判将裁定被告 Wakana Watabe 是否犯下危害人类罪。具体而言，是「清洁工」那一类的。

lines.en: : Three more janitors were found dead last week. And Kumon-mi’s district attorney, Makoto Miyamura, believes our lovable goth teacher lady is responsible!
lines.zh: : 上周又发现三名清洁工死亡。而 Kumon-mi 市的地方检察官 Makoto Miyamura 认为，我们可爱的哥特女老师就是凶手！

lines.en: : Is “lovable” really the word we’re using to describe Miss Watabe now? Isn’t her entire class afraid of her?
lines.zh: : 「可爱」这个词现在真的适合用来形容 Watabe 老师吗？她全班不都很怕她吗？

lines.en: : That just means I’m doing a good job.
lines.zh: : 那只能说明我做得很好。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest4
: Objection! Silence in the court!
lines.zh: : 反对！法庭内保持肃静！

lines.en: : Miss Imai, it’s the attorneys who call for objection. The judge is supposed to-
lines.zh: : Imai 老师，提出反对的是律师才对。法官应该——

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest5
: Objection! Badgering the judge! You trying to get on my bad side, Miyamura?!
lines.zh: : 反对！刁难法官！你是想惹我不痛快吗，Miyamura？！

lines.en: : {i}Hah...{/i}no, your honor. Please excuse my outburst.
lines.zh: : {i}哈啊……{/i}不，法官大人。请原谅我的唐突。

lines.en: : That’s what I thought!
lines.zh: : 这就对了！

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest6
: Now, prepare your opening statement! I ain’t got all day for this.
lines.zh: : 现在，准备好你的开庭陈述！我可没一整天耗在这上面。

lines.en: : Is it just me or is the judge calling the defendant “lovable” grounds for a mistrial on the case of personal bias?
lines.zh: : 是我多心了，还是法官称被告为「可爱」，已经构成了个人偏见、足以导致审判无效的理由？

lines.en: : Is it just me or is there even more bias residing within the jury itself when Ayane is responsible for the deaths of at least ten janitors?
lines.zh: : 是我多心了，还是当 Ayane 手上至少背了十条清洁工的命时，陪审团里存在着更大的偏见？

lines.en: : It is my belief that this just makes me an expert on the subject, Touka. Who would be better at spotting a janitor-killer than one who has killed janitors?
lines.zh: : 我认为这恰恰让我成为这个议题上的专家，Touka。有什么人能比一个杀过清洁工的人，更擅长识别清洁工杀手？

lines.en: : How are you so evil to the men and women who serve as the backbone of our school, but so nice to basically everyone else?
lines.zh: : 你对那些作为学校脊梁的男男女女怎么能这么恶毒，可对其他所有人又那么好？

lines.en: : It’s not like I {i}try{/i} to kill them, Noriko. I’ve been acquitted every time.
lines.zh: : 我又不是{i}故意{/i}要杀他们，Noriko。我每次都被判无罪了。

lines.en: : Is that not because you’re wealthy?
lines.zh: : 那难道不是因为你有钱吗？

lines.en: : It might be. Who’s to say?
lines.zh: : 也许是吧。谁说得准呢？

lines.en: : Miss Imai, may I ask a question?
lines.zh: : Imai 老师，我可以问个问题吗？

lines.en: : No! That’s not how this works! You speak when spoken to in this court room! You hear me, Fukuyama?!
lines.zh: : 不行！这不是这里的规矩！在这个法庭上，只有跟你说话你才能开口！听到了吗，Fukuyama？！

lines.en: : Yes, and quite clearly. You don’t have to yell.
lines.zh: : 听到了，而且很清楚。你不用吼。

lines.en: : Sorry. I love you. Miyamura! Please address the jury! Timer starts now!
lines.zh: : 抱歉。我爱你。Miyamura！请向陪审团陈词！计时开始！

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest7
: Timer? They’re being timed for this?
lines.zh: : 计时？他们这场还要计时？

lines.en: : Everyone knows the fairest court cases are those conducted under harsh time constraints with little to no prep-work done.
lines.zh: : 众所周知，最公平的法庭审判，就是那种在严苛时间限制下、几乎没做任何准备工作的。

lines.en: : You say that now, but it looks like Makoto is more than prepared for this.
lines.zh: : 你现在这么说，可看起来 Makoto 准备得相当充分。

lines.en: : Ladies and gentlemen of the jury — first and foremost, I’d like to thank you for your time.
lines.zh: : 陪审团的女士们先生们——首先，我要感谢你们抽出时间。

lines.en: : {size=-2}As a Dorm Wars contestant myself, I personally understand just how difficult it is to step away from the festivities over such a {i}serious{/i} matter when you {i}should{/i} be out having fun.{/size}
lines.zh: : {size=-2}我自己也是宿舍战争的参赛者，所以我非常理解，在这么一件严肃的事情上抽身出来、而不是出去玩有多困难。{/size}

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest8
: That raises the question, though — with such a well-known and beloved event on the cusp of arrival, what sort of person would commit such a heinous act?
lines.zh: : 那么问题来了——在这样一个众所周知、备受喜爱的活动即将到来之际，究竟是什么样的人会犯下如此滔天的罪行？

lines.en: : An act that would be all but {i}certain{/i} to disrupt such an event as it took place within these hallowed halls?
lines.zh: : 一起几乎{i}必然{/i}会扰乱这场活动的罪行，而且它恰恰就发生在这座神圣的校舍之内？

lines.en: : Ladies and gentlemen, on the night of March 1st, three janitors- no. Three {i}patriots{/i} were murdered in cold blood just two doors down from Wakana Watabe’s office.
lines.zh: : 女士们先生们，在 3 月 1 日夜里，三名清洁工——不。三名{i}爱国者{/i}被冷血谋杀，地点就在距离 Wakana Watabe 办公室两扇门之外。

lines.en: : Objection! Speculation! We don’t know that the janitors were patriots! They might have been really bad people!
lines.zh: : 反对！臆测！我们并不知道那些清洁工是爱国者！他们说不定是很坏的人！

lines.en: : Overruled! Anyone who cleans toilets is a patriot in my book! Continue, Miyamura.
lines.zh: : 驳回！在我眼里，任何刷马桶的人都是爱国者！继续，Miyamura。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest9
: Thank you, your honor. And let me say — it is not my goal to dredge up the respective {i}characters{/i} of the deceased, no.
lines.zh: : 谢谢法官大人。容我说一句——我的目的并不是要翻出死者的{i}品行{/i}为人。不是的。

lines.en: : I merely wish to bring justice to their families. And to hold the one responsible for their deaths accountable on behalf of this great city.
lines.zh: : 我只是想为他们的家属讨回公道。并代表这座伟大的城市，让那个夺走他们生命的人承担责任。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest10
: Which is precisely why I will prove without a shadow of a doubt that Wakana Watabe is {i}guilty{/i} on all three counts of murder in the first degree!
lines.zh: : 正因如此，我将毫无疑问地证明，Wakana Watabe 三项一级谋杀罪名全部{i}成立{/i}！

lines.en: : And the reason for her actions, you ask?!
lines.zh: : 而她的动机，你们要问？！

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest11
: To delay, or even worse — to {i}cancel{/i} the Dorm Wars!
lines.zh: : 为了推迟——或者更糟——为了{i}取消{/i}宿舍战争！

lines.en: : Tch. She’s good.
lines.zh: : 啧。她很厉害。

lines.en: : Just leave all the talking to me, Ms. Watabe. I’ve got it under control.
lines.zh: : 所有的话都交给我来说就好，Watabe 老师。我掌控得住。

lines.en: : Good. For that {i}is{/i} your purpose as my attorney.
lines.zh: : 好。那正{i}是{/i}你作为我的律师的用处。

lines.en: : And a purpose I shall fulfill...since it’s time to show this prosecutor how it’s done.
lines.zh: : 而那个用处我必将履行……因为是时候让这位检察官见识见识真正的本事了。

lines.en: : Uta Ushibori! Please issue your opening statement to the court!
lines.zh: : Uta Ushibori！请向法庭作出你的开庭陈述！

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest12
: Ladies and gentlemen of the jury!
lines.zh: : 陪审团的女士们先生们！

lines.en: : No!
: What?
lines.zh: : 什么？

lines.en: : Ushibori! Are you admitting that your client {i}is{/i} responsible for the murder of the three janitors?!
lines.zh: : Ushibori！你{i}是{/i}在承认你的当事人犯下了谋杀三名清洁工的罪行吗？！

lines.en: : Quite the contrary, Miss Imai! Wakana Watabe would never even {i}consider{/i} an act as heinous as murder.
lines.zh: : 恰恰相反，Imai 老师！Wakana Watabe 绝不会去{i}考虑{/i}谋杀这种滔天的行为。

lines.en: : Which is why I find the purpose of an opening statement rather pointless. Especially when Makoto’s gonna be a big smartypants about it.
lines.zh: : 所以我才觉得开庭陈述这种东西毫无意义。尤其当 Makoto 非要摆出一副聪明鬼样子的时候。

lines.en: : Objection! Argumentative!
lines.zh: : 反对！挑衅性提问！

lines.en: : Nuh-uh!
lines.zh: : 才不是！

lines.en: : Objection sustained. Uta Ushibori, the court orders you to provide an opening statement because it’s a part of the competition.
lines.zh: : 反对成立。Uta Ushibori，本庭命令你提交开庭陈述，因为这是比赛的一部分。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest13
: Tch. Fine. But you’ll all see within a matter of seconds that asking for one is rather pointless when the truth is as plain as day!
lines.zh: : 啧。行吧。不过几秒钟之内你们就会明白，当真相如同白日一般昭然若揭时，要这么个陈述有多没意义！

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest14
: Wakana Watabe does not have the {i}energy{/i} to murder anyone! She barely has the energy to get out of her chair!
lines.zh: : Wakana Watabe 根本没有那个{i}精力{/i}去谋杀任何人！她连从椅子上站起来的力气都快没了！

lines.en: : Do you really believe a woman like that is capable of murder?!
lines.zh: : 你们真觉得那样的女人有能力杀人吗？！

lines.en: : Objection! Lack of foundation, your honor.
lines.zh: : 反对！缺乏依据，法官大人。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest15
: Shut up! You think you’re such a good lawyer just because you know stuff about being a lawyer?! As if!
lines.zh: : 闭嘴！你以为自己就因为懂点律师的事儿就算个好律师了吗？！才怪！

lines.en: : Miyamura, elaborate.
lines.zh: : Miyamura，详细说明。

lines.en: : Your honor, the defense fails to provide any factual evidence supporting the claim that Miss Watabe lacks energy when she could merely be {i}acting{/i} tired.
lines.zh: : 法官大人，辩方未能提供任何事实证据，来支持 Watabe 老师缺乏精力这一主张——她很可能只是在{i}装{/i}累。

lines.en: : Overruled. She called me over to her apartment once just to tie her shoes since she didn’t want to bend down.
lines.zh: : 驳回。她有一次把我叫到她公寓，就为了替她系鞋带，因为她不想弯腰。

lines.en: : And you came. Because you knew I wouldn’t murder you.
lines.zh: : 而你还真来了。因为你知道我不会杀你。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest16
: Objection! I told my client to let me do the talking and now she suddenly isn’t! There are probably rules against that.
lines.zh: : 反对！我明明让我的当事人让我来说话，可她突然又不听了！大概有规定不许这样。

lines.en: : Overruled! The defendant is a strong, independent woman and is allowed to speak if she wants to!
lines.zh: : 驳回！被告是一位坚强独立的女性，想说话就可以说！

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest17
: But-
lines.zh: : 可是——

lines.en: : Order in the court! I don’t have a gavel though, so just pretend I’m banging it right now.
lines.zh: : 法庭肃静！不过我没有法槌，所以就当我在敲它吧。

lines.en: : My, this is just like the daytime television programming I used to watch with my mother when I was younger. Just without all of the poverty.
lines.zh: : 哎呀，这简直就像我小时候和母亲一起看的那些日间电视节目。只是没有那么多贫穷。

lines.en: : What do you think the chances are of them actually being able to provide any sort of evidence in a clearly fictional case?
lines.zh: : 你们觉得，在一个明显虚构的案子里，她们真能拿出什么证据吗？

lines.en: : Evidence seldom matters at all if a lawyer is good enough at manipulating the jury. And I imagine that’s the card Uta’s going to play based on her experience with people.
lines.zh: : 如果一个律师足够擅长操纵陪审团，证据根本就不重要。而以 Uta 与人打交道的经验，我想她要打的就是这张牌。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest18
: You mean at the maid cafe? You think she’s going to try and manipulate us the way she does her customers?
lines.zh: : 你是说在女仆咖啡厅？你觉得她会像对付客人那样来操纵我们？

lines.en: : I don’t have any evidence to support that claim. And I may be biased as well given that Makoto is a resident of our floor. But that’s what I would do if I was her.
lines.zh: : 我没有任何证据支持这个说法。而且我也可能有偏见，毕竟 Makoto 住在我们这层楼。但如果我是她，我会那么做。

lines.en: : Do you watch courtroom TV too, Futaba? You’ve seemed pretty engrossed in all of this since the moment we sat down.
lines.zh: : Futaba 你也看庭审剧吗？从坐下那一刻起你就一直看得挺入迷。

lines.en: : Not really. Rin and I used to play Ace Attorney together in middle school, though. It’s likely just residual interest from that.
lines.zh: : 不太看。不过 Rin 和我初中时一起玩过《逆转裁判》。大概就是那之后残留的兴趣吧。

lines.en: : What is this “Ace Attorney” you speak of? Some type of role playing game similar to the one we saw in the cafeteria earlier?
lines.zh: : 你说的这个「逆转裁判」是什么？是某种角色扮演游戏，就像我们之前在食堂看到的那种？

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest19
: It’s a video game series...where you...solve silly court cases and...stuff like that.
lines.zh: : 是个电子游戏系列……就是……解决一些傻乎乎的法庭案件和……那一类的东西。

lines.en: : It’s also the virtual home of Miles Edgeworth — who may or may not be the first cartoon character I ever had a crush on.
lines.zh: : 那也是 Miles Edgeworth 的虚拟故乡——他大概算是我第一个心动过的卡通角色。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest20
: Mine was Mordecai from the Regular Show. I never had any idea what he was saying because I don’t speak English, but that voice just does it for me.
lines.zh: : 我的是《日常参考》里的 Mordecai。我因为不会英语，从来听不懂他在说什么，可那个声音就是很戳我。

lines.en: : I liked Edward from Full Metal Alchemist.
lines.zh: : 我喜欢《钢之炼金术师》里的 Edward。

lines.en: : I don’t know literally any of these things.
lines.zh: : 这些东西我一个都不知道。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest21
: Did you never watch cartoons growing up, Touka?
lines.zh: : 你小时候从来没看过动画片吗，Touka？

lines.en: : Animated television? Not that I can remember. I was taught that sort of content can rot one’s brain. It’s the same reason I avoid the Internet.
lines.zh: : 动画电视节目？据我所知没有。我受的教育是那类内容会腐蚀人的大脑。就像我避开互联网是同一个理由。

lines.en: : That’s fair and you should probably keep it that way.
lines.zh: : 那也合理，你大概该继续保持下去。

lines.en: : Yeah, probably. You’re missing out on a lot of hot cartoon characters, though. And an entire genre of porn.
lines.zh: : 嗯，大概吧。不过你错过了好多很火的卡通角色。还有一整个类型的色情作品。

lines.en: : Interesting. I’m learning about all sorts of interesting fetishes lately. This is the first I’m hearing of people being attracted to cartoons, though.
lines.zh: : 有意思。我最近真是了解到各种各样的奇妙癖好了。不过被人喜欢上卡通角色这种事，我还是第一次听说。

lines.en: : Oh, it’s super common! And not at all weird. Even if it’s for something that {i}sounds{/i} weird. Like ponies.
lines.zh: : 哦，那超级常见！而且一点也不奇怪。就算{i}听起来{/i}奇怪的东西也一样。比如小马。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest22
: Ponies?...
: Yup! Not weird at all. Right, girls? Sana is wrong.
lines.zh: : 对！一点都不奇怪。对吧，各位？Sana 是错的。

lines.en: : I’m just happy that {i}you’re{/i} happy, Noriko.
lines.zh: : {i}你{/i}开心就好，Noriko。

lines.en: : Huh...yes, I do believe it’s good that I was kept away from animated media in hindsight.
lines.zh: : 嗯……是啊，现在想来，我一直被隔绝在动画媒体之外，或许是件好事。

lines.en: : Oh, right. Court is in session. We should probably be paying attention to that.
lines.zh: : 哦对。庭审还在进行。我们大概该把注意力放回去。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest23
: ...which is why I can’t help but be appalled, your honor! {i}Nineteen{/i} children are without a parent now!
lines.zh: : ……因此我不得不感到震惊，法官大人！现在有{i}十九{/i}个孩子失去了父母！

lines.en: : That’s close to the same amount of parents missing from girls in our class when assuming that the ones we know very little about, like Maya and Yasu, are missing {i}at least{/i} one!
lines.zh: : 这和我们班上父母缺失的女生数量差不多——前提是算上像 Maya 和 Yasu 那样我们所知甚少的人，她们{i}至少{/i}也缺一个家长！

lines.en: : Objection! Irrelevant! But also very sad!
lines.zh: : 反对！无关！不过也太让人难过了！

lines.en: : Sustained! And also very sad!
lines.zh: : 成立！而且确实太让人难过了！

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest24
: Ladies and gentlemen of the jury, the fact remains that the bodies of all three deceased were found just several steps from Miss Watabe’s door!
lines.zh: : 陪审团的女士们先生们，事实依然是——三名死者的尸体全都在离 Watabe 老师门口只有几步远的地方被发现！

lines.en: : And if the discovery period was longer than ten hours, I’d be able to show you sufficient proof that their DNA was found {i}in her office.{/i}
lines.zh: : 而且如果证据开示期超过十小时，我就能向你们出示充分的证明，表明他们的 DNA 出现在了{i}她的办公室里{/i}。

lines.en: : Objection! Something else probably! I don’t know what it’s called, though!
lines.zh: : 反对！大概是别的什么吧！不过我不知道那叫什么！

lines.en: : Sustained, probably! All I know is that it ain’t real evidence if it hasn’t gone through that discovery thing!
lines.zh: : 大概成立！我只知道，没经过那个开示程序的就不是真证据！

lines.en: : Which I understand! But when all other roads lead back to her, you {i}must{/i} begin to question her involvement!
lines.zh: : 这点我理解！但当所有其他的线索都指向她时，你就{i}必须{/i}开始质疑她的涉案程度了！

lines.en: : If she is not the murderer herself, which is {i}highly{/i} unlikely based on the evidence the city of Kumon-mi has gathered, she is, at bare minimum, an accomplice.
lines.zh: : 如果她本人不是凶手——基于 Kumon-mi 市收集的证据，这种可能性{i}极低{/i}——那么她至少也是个共犯。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest25
: Your honor — the defense would like to move to cross-examination as the prosecutor herself now acknowledges the possibility that my client {i}is{/i} innocent.
lines.zh: : 法官大人——鉴于检察官本人现在也承认我的当事人有可能{i}是{/i}无辜的，辩方请求进入交叉询问环节。

lines.en: : {size=-3}Should we take her words at face value, we can make the astute observation that this argument is built upon nothing but emotion and the desire to scapegoat my client for something she just happened to be nearby for.{/size}
lines.zh: : {size=-3}如果我们只从表面理解她的话，就能敏锐地观察到：这套论点完全建立在情绪之上，以及想为一件她只是恰好在场的事情找替罪羊的欲望之上。{/size}

lines.en: : Why did you wait until now to start sounding smart? Miyamura has been wiping the floor with you so far.
lines.zh: : 你为什么等到现在才开始听起来像回事？Miyamura 到目前为止一直把你按在地上摩擦。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest26
: Objection! Favoritism, your honor! My client clearly likes Makoto more than me!
lines.zh: : 反对！偏袒，法官大人！我的当事人显然更喜欢 Makoto！

lines.en: : Overruled. The defense cannot object to itself. The court will now move to cross-examination and asks the prosecution to call upon its first witness.
lines.zh: : 驳回。辩方不能反对自己。本庭现在进入交叉询问环节，并请控方传唤第一位证人。

lines.en: : There are witnesses?! Why didn’t anyone inform me of this?!
lines.zh: : 有证人？！为什么没人通知我这件事？！

lines.en: : Your honor, the prosecution asks that one {i}Akira Arakawa{/i} takes the stand.
lines.zh: : 法官大人，控方请求 {i}Akira Arakawa{/i} 出庭作证。

lines.en: : Oh, okay. Well, I guess I don’t have to worry about who knows my name and who doesn’t anymore.
lines.zh: : 哦，好。那我大概不用再担心谁知道我的名字、谁不知道了。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest27
: Mr. Arakawa — you would consider yourself {i}friends{/i} with Wakana Watabe, would you not?
lines.zh: : Arakawa 先生——你自认为与 Wakana Watabe 是{i}朋友{/i}，对吗？

lines.en: : We’re just coworkers, really.
lines.zh: : 我们其实只是同事。

lines.en: : Fuck you, Arakawa. I’ll kill you too.
lines.zh: : 去你的，Arakawa。我连你也一起杀。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest28
: O-Objection! The defense asks for Miss Watabe’s most recent outburst to be stricken from the record!
lines.zh: : 反……反对！辩方请求将 Watabe 老师刚才那句发作从记录中删去！

lines.en: : Sustained! We don’t have a stenographer, so there {i}isn’t{/i} a record! Here’s hoping the jury was paying attention!
lines.zh: : 成立！我们没有速记员，所以根本{i}没有{/i}记录！希望陪审团刚才有在认真听！

lines.en: : Hm? What? Are we voting now?
lines.zh: : 嗯？什么？我们现在要投票了吗？

lines.en: : Did Miss Watabe just admit to being guilty?
lines.zh: : Watabe 老师刚刚是承认有罪了吗？

lines.en: : She might have. She doesn’t {i}look{/i} very guilty, though.
lines.zh: : 也许是吧。不过她{i}看起来{/i}不太像有罪的样子。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest29
: {i}Miss Watabe! Your attorney advises you keep your mouth shut unless it’s to preach your innocence!{/i}
lines.zh: : {i}Watabe 老师！你的律师建议你闭嘴，除非是要宣讲你的清白！{/i}

lines.en: : Miyamura had the whole case figured out the moment she said this was done to have the Dorm Wars canceled.
lines.zh: : 从 Miyamura 说出「这是为了让宿舍战争取消而做的」那一刻起，整件案子她就已经看透了。

lines.en: : If I had known it would only make me more involved, I would have just killed myself instead.
lines.zh: : 如果我早知道这只会让我陷得更深，我还不如直接自杀算了。

lines.en: : Objection! The Dorm Wars is fun!
lines.zh: : 反对！宿舍战争很好玩的！

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest30
: Are you objecting to {i}me?!{/i} You useless attorney! Call for a recess and negotiate a plea deal!
lines.zh: : 你在反对{i}我{/i}？！你这没用的律师！申请休庭去谈认罪协议！

lines.en: : Your honor! The defense asks that the prosecution continue its cross examination!
lines.zh: : 法官大人！辩方请求控方继续交叉询问！

lines.en: : So...no recess?
lines.zh: : 所以……不休庭？

lines.en: : No! I want to ask Sensei stuff too! This is fun!
lines.zh: : 不！我也想问 Sensei 问题！这多好玩啊！

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest31
: Anyway, as I was saying, you’re friends with Wakana Watabe. Which means you know her better than most, correct?
lines.zh: : 总之，正如我刚才所说，你和 Wakana Watabe 是朋友。也就是说，你比大多数人更了解她，对吗？

lines.en: : She cried into my shoulder once and it was really cute. She also smells nice and has a great body. It just doesn’t work very well.
lines.zh: : 她有一次趴在我肩膀上哭，真的很可爱。她闻起来也很香，身材也很好。只是那副身体不太听使唤。

lines.en: : Don’t fucking tell them that I {i}cried,{/i} Arakawa! I can’t look weak in front of these miscreants!
lines.zh: : 别他妈告诉她们我{i}哭过{/i}，Arakawa！我不能在你们这帮混蛋面前显得软弱！

lines.en: : And while Miss Watabe was crying into your shoulder, did she by any chance confess to the murder of three individuals?
lines.zh: : 那么，当 Watabe 老师趴在你肩膀上哭的时候，她有没有向你坦白过谋杀三个人的事？

lines.en: : Uhh...not that I can recall.
lines.zh: : 呃……我想不起来。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest32
: Ladies and gentlemen of the jury, take special note of that wording. “Not that I can recall.”
lines.zh: : 陪审团的女士们先生们，请特别留意那个措辞。「我想不起来。」

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest31
: You acknowledge that your memory is worse than most, correct?
lines.zh: : 你承认自己的记忆力比大多数人差，对吗？

lines.en: : That’s...right.
lines.zh: : 是……没错。

lines.en: : So it’s possible Miss Watabe {i}did{/i} confess her crimes to you and you just...don’t remember. Correct?
lines.zh: : 所以，Watabe 老师有可能{i}确实{/i}向你坦白过她的罪行，而你只是……不记得了。对吗？

lines.en: : I...guess that’s technically correct. Sure.
lines.zh: : 我……想从技术上说是对的。算是吧。

lines.en: : And what do you think it would take to...jog your memory? A photo? A video?
lines.zh: : 那你觉得，需要什么才能……唤起你的记忆？一张照片？一段视频？

lines.en: : The promise for one to destroy a pre-filled marriage contract that may or may not be hidden away in a safe somewhere?
lines.zh: : 或者承诺替你销毁一份可能藏在某处保险箱里的、已经填好的结婚申请书？

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest33
: You know, it’s starting to come back to me-
lines.zh: : 你知道吗，我开始想起来了——

lines.en: : No it’s not! And it’s the defense’s turn now!
lines.zh: : 不你没有！而且现在轮到辩方了！

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest34
: Akira Arakawa — on a scale of one to ten, how cute do you think I am?
lines.zh: : Akira Arakawa——一到十分，你觉得我有多可爱？

lines.en: : Ten.
lines.zh: : 十分。

lines.en: : Objection! Relevance, your honor. This line of questioning has nothing to do with the case. The defense is clearly leading the witness and-
lines.zh: : 反对！关联性，法官大人。这一连串提问与本案无关。辩方显然在诱导证人，而且——

lines.en: : Overruled! You’ve objected too many times!
lines.zh: : 驳回！你反对太多次了！

lines.en: : There’s a limit?!
lines.zh: : 还有次数限制？！

lines.en: : And do you believe I’ll make a great wife one day?
lines.zh: : 那你觉不觉得，我有一天会成为一位出色的妻子？

lines.en: : You definitely seem built for that, yeah.
lines.zh: : 你看起来确实是为那个而生的，嗯。

lines.en: : And assuming we were both legal consenting adults, would you have any issue taking my hand in marriage?
lines.zh: : 那么假设我们都是达到法定年龄、能够表示同意的成年人，你会介意娶我为妻吗？

lines.en: : I mean...that’s a complicated-
lines.zh: : 我是说……那挺复杂——

lines.en: : Just a yes or no is fine, thank you.
lines.zh: : 只要回答是或不是就好，谢谢。

lines.en: : Then...yes?
scene courtroomcontest35
: Your honor, this witness is clearly biased and involved in a conflict of interest. The defense calls for him to be expelled from the stand so the court can move to recess.
lines.zh: : 法官大人，该证人显然存在偏见，并牵涉利益冲突。辩方请求将他逐出证人席，以便本庭进入休庭。

lines.en: : Oh, you bitch.
lines.zh: : 哦，你这贱人。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest36
: Interesting strategy.
lines.zh: : 有意思的策略。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest37
: Unfortunately though, it appears as if the jury is already prepared to provide a verdict and that we don’t need to dismiss the court at all.
lines.zh: : 不过很遗憾，陪审团似乎已经准备好作出裁决，我们根本不需要解散法庭。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest38
: What?! No!
lines.zh: : 什么？！不！

lines.en: : Foreperson Fukuyama! How does the jury find the defendant?!
lines.zh: : 首席陪审员 Fukuyama！陪审团对被告的裁定是什么？！

lines.en: : In the case of the city of Kumon-mi vs Wakana Watabe — we, the jury, find the defendant to be {i}guilty{/i} on all three counts of murder in the first degree.
lines.zh: : 在 Kumon-mi 市 诉 Wakana Watabe 一案中——我们陪审团裁定被告三项一级谋杀罪名全部{i}成立{/i}。

lines.en: : On what grounds?!
lines.zh: : 凭什么？！

lines.en: : On the grounds that she confessed to being guilty on all three counts of murder in the first degree.
lines.zh: : 凭她承认了自己三项一级谋杀罪名全部成立。

lines.en: : Gah! All you had to do was keep your mouth shut, Miss Watabe!
lines.zh: : 啊！你只要闭嘴就行了啊，Watabe 老师！

lines.en: : No, you still probably would have lost either way.
lines.zh: : 不，反正你大概还是会输。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest39
: The court rules in favor of Kumon-mi and sentences Wakana Watabe to a $100 fine payable in either food or alcohol at her earliest convenience.
lines.zh: : 本庭判 Kumon-mi 市胜诉，并判处 Wakana Watabe 罚款 100 美元，可在方便之时以食物或酒精支付。

lines.en: : Three counts of murder and all she gets is a $100 fine?
lines.zh: : 三项谋杀罪，她只被罚 100 美元？

lines.en: : I’m tellin’ you guys! The system’s broken! They don’t care about the common man! We want justice for the families of those three janitors!
lines.zh: : 我跟你们说！这系统烂透了！他们根本不关心普通人！我们要为那三名清洁工的家属讨回公道！

lines.en: : Fine. The charge is increased to $300 effective immediately. Court is now adjourned.
lines.zh: : 行。罚金即刻上调至 300 美元。现在休庭。

lines.en: scene black
: Boom! Justice achieved! This is why ya rise up, girls.
lines.zh: : 砰！正义得到了伸张！这就是为什么我们要站起来啊，姑娘们。

lines.en: : I don’t know...I still feel like the charge is a little light.
lines.zh: : 我不知道……我还是觉得这判罚有点太轻了。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest40
: You know, ignoring the fact that Wakana basically just got away with murder, that went a lot better than I would have expected after hearing about a mock court case in school.
lines.zh: : 你知道吗，撇开 Wakana 基本上就是逃过了谋杀指控这件事不谈，比我听说学校里要办模拟法庭时预想的要好太多了。

lines.en: : Makocchi was great. I probably should’ve taken it a little more seriously, though.
lines.zh: : Makocchi 很棒。不过我大概本该更认真一点的。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest41
: Makocchi?
lines.zh: : Makocchi？

lines.en: : Your nickname!
lines.zh: : 你的昵称啊！

lines.en: : Interesting. I’m not used to nicknames that aren’t inherently hurtful.
lines.zh: : 有意思。我不太习惯那种不带恶意的昵称。

lines.en: : What’s the plan now? Why are you two just waiting around out here? Looks like everybody else went home already.
lines.zh: : 现在什么计划？你们俩为什么还在这儿干等着？看起来其他人都已经回去了。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest42
: Nobody went home! They’re all heading over to Koi Cafe for the next tournament.
lines.zh: : 没人回去！她们都去 Koi Cafe 参加下一场比赛了。

lines.en: : Which is...what exactly?
lines.zh: : 那是……具体是什么比赛？

lines.en: : Another stand-up comedy showdown. Which is why we wouldn’t hold it against you if you didn’t want to come since the last one got really weird.
lines.zh: : 又一场单口喜剧对决。所以如果你不想来，我们也不会怪你——毕竟上一场变得很奇怪。

lines.en: : But if you {i}did{/i} want to come, we’d be happy if you walked there with us! And if you stay in the center, you can hold both of our hands at once!
lines.zh: : 但如果你{i}想{/i}来，我们会很高兴你和我们走过去！而且如果你走中间，还能同时牵着我们俩的手！

lines.en: : Who is...competing exactly?
lines.zh: : 参赛的……到底是谁？

lines.en: : Not Tsuneyo if that’s what you’re worried about.
lines.zh: : 如果你担心的话，不是 Tsuneyo。

lines.en: : It’s Futaba and Touka this time — two of the least controversial girls we have! Who are, somewhat coincidentally, probably not going to be very funny.
lines.zh: : 这次是 Futaba 和 Touka——我们有史以来最没有争议的两个女生！而且颇为巧合的是，她们大概也不会很好笑。

lines.en: : Which is why we think you {i}should{/i} come with us. And praise us both along the way for how exceptional and smart we were just now.
lines.zh: : 所以我们认为你应{i}该{/i}跟我们一起来。而且一路上要夸我们俩刚才有多出色、多聪明。

lines.en: : Just think, Sensei! How many more opportunities will you ever have to praise {i}me{/i} for being smart?
lines.zh: : 想想看，Sensei！你这辈子还能有几回机会夸{i}我{/i}聪明？

lines.en: : You guys don’t need to convince me. I’ll join you. I could use some coffee after all of today’s...{i}excitement{/i} anyway.
lines.zh: : 你们不用说服我。我跟你们去。反正经历了今天这些……{i}刺激{/i}，我也该喝点咖啡了。

lines.en: : Are you happy to be back? Wanna come out of retirement and give Makoto somebody to follow around like a puppy again?
lines.zh: : 你回来开心吗？想不想复出，重新让 Makoto 有个能像小狗一样跟着的人？

lines.en: : I’d say she’s more of an overly-obedient service dog than a puppy. Which I assumed Imani was getting to experience now in place of me.
lines.zh: : 我觉得她与其说是小狗，不如说是过度服从的导盲犬。我本来以为现在轮到 Imani 代替我体验这个了。

lines.en: : Imani’s actually good at her job, so she doesn’t {i}need{/i} as much help.
lines.zh: : Imani 其实很擅长她的工作，所以她不{i}需要{/i}那么多帮助。

lines.en: : I figured. Which is why it’s weird that you two want me back at all.
lines.zh: : 我想也是。所以你们俩还想让我回来，才显得奇怪。

lines.en: : There’s nothing weird about wanting to spend more time with the boy you like. Right, Makoto?
lines.zh: : 想和喜欢的男孩子多待一会儿，没什么好奇怪的。对吧，Makoto？

lines.en: : Exactly. And I think it’s fine to let my grades {i}suffer{/i} a little bit given the circumstances of everything. Right, Sensei?
lines.zh: : 没错。而且我觉得，鉴于当下的种种情况，让我的成绩稍微{i}下滑{/i}一点也没关系。对吧，Sensei？

lines.en: : So you two just...you’re openly competing now?
lines.zh: : 所以你们俩现在就……公开竞争了？

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest43
: Most of us are, yeah.
lines.zh: : 我们大多数人都是，嗯。

lines.en: : The majority of the class has accepted by now that we’re active participants in a perpetual battle for your heart.
lines.zh: : 全班大部分人现在都已经接受了这样一个事实：我们都是一场争夺你的心的永恒之战中的积极参与者。

lines.en: : So some of us are forming alliances while others are contacting the black market to find out which organs sell for the most money.
lines.zh: : 所以有些人正在结盟，另一些人则在联系黑市，打听哪个器官能卖最多的钱。

lines.en: : Hearts go for about a million US dollars — which is fun because they’re also the most poetic organ to harvest when fighting a battle for someone’s love.
lines.zh: : 心脏大概能卖一百万美元——这很有意思，因为在为某个人的爱而战时，心脏也是最富有诗意的采摘器官。

lines.en: : Please don’t make this a thing that just...everyone’s okay with.
lines.zh: : 请别把这件事变成一种……大家都习以为常的东西。

lines.en: scene courtroomcontest44
: We hide it from the other teachers if that’s what you’re worried about.
lines.zh: : 如果你担心的是那个，我们在其他老师面前是藏着掖着的。

lines.en: : Though, I’ll be the first to admit that things {i}do{/i} become a little obvious with Miss Imai around sometimes. We should probably hide that better.
lines.zh: : 不过我得第一个承认，有时候 Imai 老师在场，事情就会{i}变得{/i}有点明显。我们大概该藏得更好些。

lines.en: : You should hide it from {i}each other{/i} too.
lines.zh: : 你们也该{i}互相{/i}瞒着点。

lines.en: : I don’t want any of you ruining your relationships over someone like me when I never should have dragged you into my life in the first place.
lines.zh: : 我不想看到你们任何人为了我这样的人毁掉自己的人际关系，更何况我一开始根本就不该把你们拖进我的人生。

lines.en: : Probably not. But we’re glad that you did.
lines.zh: : 大概是不该。但我们很高兴你那么做了。

lines.en: : You think I’d wear a skirt this tight for just anybody?
lines.zh: : 你以为我随便给谁都会穿这么紧的裙子吗？

lines.en: : Don’t actually answer that question. It’ll only hurt my feelings.
lines.zh: : 别真的回答那个问题。那只会伤到我的感情。

lines.en: : ...I’ll walk with you guys.
lines.zh: : ……我跟你们走。

lines.en: scene black
: I just ask that you don’t make this feel {i}normal{/i} for me.
lines.zh: : 我只求你们别让这件事对我来说变得「{i}正常{/i}」。

lines.en: : It’s not the same if I have nothing to fear.
lines.zh: : 如果我无所畏惧，那就不一样了。
